title: Fix or delete NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile's fragile non-null-Object emptiness check — fallbackProfileId branch is effectively unreachable and untested
rule: Type-safety design flaw in dead code
why: profileIdOrRow is typed as non-nullable Object, so it can never be null, and Object.toString() is non-empty for every realistic value (an int, a non-empty String, or the default 'Instance of X') — the only way to hit the fallbackProfileId branch is to pass a literal empty string, which is nowhere documented as the sentinel. This reads like an attempt to model 'optional row value, else use this id' that should have used `Object?` with a null check instead of a string-emptiness check. It has zero callers repo-wide (confirmed via grep across lib/ and test/), so this has never been exercised and the bug would surface silently the moment someone starts using it expecting the fallback to work.
recommendation: If kept, change the signature to `Object? profileIdOrRow` and check `== null` instead of `.toString().isNotEmpty`. If truly unused going forward, delete it along with the other 5 unused factories (see companion finding).
acceptance_criteria: If kept: a unit test constructs NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile with profileIdOrRow omitted/null and asserts the fallbackProfileId branch actually executes
If deleted: covered by the companion 'unused factories' finding's acceptance criteria
